subject: National literals
notes: kb/Work PB160 (wave 1091 G). cite.py --check 8.3.3.5.4 "The implementor defines the result of specifying a hex-character-sequence-1 for which no corresponding character in that coded character set exists." -> OK §8.3.3.5.4 5) (General rules). The implementor's definition is now written AND pinned. HALF 1 (no corresponding character): CobolLiteral.DecodeHexGroups stores each four-digit group verbatim as its UTF-16 code unit, a surrogate half or noncharacter included - one character position, no diagnostic, no exception condition; documented in docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-97 (A.1 item 97, cite.py --check A.1 "Hexadecimal national literals (mapping for non-existing corresponding character)" -> OK §A.1 97), and the code comment now carries the GR5 citation. Re-probed on the wave-1091 build (tests/conformance/2002/l1c12_hex_national_no_character.cob at --std 2002): LEN:1 2 / ORD:55297 65536 00066 / ORD:55297 56321 / GT / [U+FFFD] / NO-EC, exactly the golden, which pins LENGTH(NX"D800") = 1, ORD of D800/FFFF/0041 and of a valid pair's halves, the code-unit comparison and the U+FFFD DISPLAY of a lone DC00 under >>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON. HALF 2 (characters not a multiple of four bits): the condition cannot arise - a national character is one 16-bit code unit from exactly four digits (§8.3.3.5.3 SR5, DOC-A.1-122) - documented in DOC-A.1-98. The golden's code-unit comparison was rewritten from two literals (IF NX"FFFF" > NX"D800", COBOL3146 under §8.8.4.2.1, cite.py OK §8.8.4.2.1 13)) to a data-item subject (IF WS-N(2:1) > NX"D800"), so the witness is conforming source. Editions: NX literals are a COBOL-2002 introduction; at COBOL-85 the construct is rejected COBOL0900 (negative r03-hex-national-literal-at-85). (A.1 item 97's own parenthetical still says "General rule 4" - a renumbering residue in the spec; the rule is GR5 in the body text.)
